candidates.source_name: Komerční banka – Dodavatelé (supplier hub, cs)
candidates.why_relevant: KB's only public supplier-facing page. Hosts the binding contractual stack a vendor must accept: Všeobecné obchodní podmínky pro dodavatele (004, eff. 1/7/2021), Charta odpovědného nákupu, SG Group Code of Conduct, Anti-Corruption Code, plus category-specific annexes (training providers 003, construction works 002, IT security clauses for cloud, GDPR personal-data transfer template, obligations of external collaborators using KB's information system). candidates.source_name: Erste Group Procurement (EGP) – subsidiary and general supplier pages
candidates.why_relevant: Highest-value structural finding for Česká spořitelna. ČS does not run an independent public supplier portal; its external spend is managed by Erste Group Procurement, a Vienna-headquartered shared-service company with its OWN SUBSIDIARY IN THE CZECH REPUBLIC. EGP states it manages the whole external spend of all majority-owned Erste entities and splits activity into Sourcing (strategic, category/supplier management), Tactical Purchasing (low-value) and Order Management (call-offs from existing contracts) — a category-level map of how a ČS deal is actually routed. It also operates a standardised supplier onboarding process anchored on a Supplier Code of Conduct, and the general page offers supplier documents (Code of Conduct, General Terms and Conditions of Purchase) translated per country via a country drop-down, so a Czech-language ČS supplier pack should be reachable there.
candidates.access_status: open; country supplier documents behind a JS drop-down (needs a rendering fetch)

Also resolve the Czech EGP legal entity in the CZ commercial register (justice.cz / ARES) to get its ICO, registered address and filed financials — that entity is the real ČS buying counterparty.

negative_findings.description: Česká spořitelna (csas.cz) appears to have NO 'pro dodavatele' / supplier section at all. Czech-language searches combining csas.cz with dodavatel, nákup, kodex dodavatele, portál dodavatele, sourcing, and výběrové řízení returned only unrelated client-facing content (e-Faktura, eFactoring, ESG guidance sold to corporate clients) plus third-party pages. The Erste Group Procurement finding explains why: ČS external spend is handled by the group procurement shared service, which has its own Czech subsidiary.
negative_findings.result_summary: No csas.cz supplier/procurement URL identified across four cs and en query variants; the function is confirmed to sit at Erste Group Procurement instead.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: Anyone hunting for a ČS supplier portal will find nothing and may wrongly conclude ČS does not tender. The correct target is the Erste Group Procurement CZ entity, not csas.cz — a routing correction that changes where the whole ČS demand signal is watched.

negative_findings.description: Every csob.cz URL I attempted returned HTTP 500 Internal Server Error — both https://www.csob.cz/dodavatele and the procurement policy PDF at /documents/10710/927640/procurement-politika-vztahu-s-dodavateli-en.pdf, the latter having appeared as a live search result. A uniform 500 across unrelated paths is characteristic of bot defence or edge-layer filtering, not of missing documents.
negative_findings.result_summary: csob.cz: 2/2 fetch attempts returned HTTP 500. Content confirmed to exist via search index and via a Czech third-party interview describing the same policy. Recorded as unverified, NOT dead.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: ČSOB is the largest CZ bank by assets and a core target of this cell. If the collector is a plain HTTP client it will silently fail on the whole csob.cz estate and the bank will look sourceless. The pipeline needs a headless-browser fetch path for this domain.

negative_findings.description: No supplier, procurement, or vendor-onboarding page found for Air Bank, Partners Banka, or Fio banka. Czech-language searching (dodavatelé, nákup, výběrové řízení, dodavatel, spolupráce) returned only retail-product and press content. For Air Bank the nearest artefact is the PPF Group / Home Credit Code of Ethics, which mentions an Air Bank ethics reporting mailbox but says nothing about procurement. Fio banka, as a domestically owned bank with no foreign parent, publishes no supplier instrument at all.
negative_findings.result_summary: Three of eight target banks yield zero supplier-channel sources in either language.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: Coverage of this cell is intrinsically capped at roughly five of eight banks via web sources. Air Bank/Fio demand signal must be reached by other means (register filings, staff mapping, trade press, direct contact), not by portal monitoring.

negative_findings.description: UniCredit Bank Czech Republic and Slovakia has no locatable CZ supplier/procurement page. Searches in cs and en returned only client-facing material — the Global Transaction Banking country page, a merchant acquiring portal (merchantportal-unicredit-cz.posmansuite.com, which is a POS-merchant service, NOT a supplier portal), the API developer catalogue, and directory entries. A follow-up en search for a UniCredit group-level 'suppliers portal' returned no UniCredit-owned result at all, only generic vendor-portal marketing.
negative_findings.result_summary: No UniCredit CZ or UniCredit Group supplier portal URL established in two targeted searches.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: Risk of a false positive: the merchant portal is superficially portal-shaped and could be miscatalogued as a supplier channel. It is not. UniCredit is currently the weakest-covered systemic bank in this cell.

negative_findings.description: Across all eight target banks I found no instance of a published RFP, tender notice, or award notice on a bank's own site. Supplier-facing publication is uniformly limited to policy artefacts: codes of conduct, general purchase terms, ESG/responsible-purchasing charters. The one confirmed tender mention for a target bank — Česká spořitelna's tender for the sale of a receivables portfolio, reported by Patria — is an asset disposal, i.e. the bank selling, not buying, and so falls outside supplier-side procurement.
negative_findings.result_summary: Zero buy-side tender or award notices located on any of the eight banks' own channels.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: Sets realistic expectations for workstream A2 in CZ: private-bank cells produce policy and process intelligence, never notice-level demand data. Pipelines built to parse award notices will return empty for this cell no matter how well they are tuned.

negative_findings.description: For no target bank could I confirm the named e-sourcing platform through which RFx invitations are actually issued. Leads only: SG references a 'Sourcing Hub' e-sourcing portal (KB's parent) but publishes no entry URL; RBI is documented on akirolabs category management with an ORACLE iProcurement-based e-auction reference in secondary reporting; Erste Group Procurement describes a standardised onboarding process but names no tool; ČSOB is described only as accepting offers electronically. Attempts to tie any bank to Ariba, Jaggaer, Coupa or Ivalua produced no primary evidence.
negative_findings.result_summary: 0/8 banks with a confirmed, named, entry-point-resolved sourcing platform; 3 partial leads, all secondary or unnamed.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: The sourcing platform is the chokepoint where demand becomes visible to an invited vendor. Not knowing it means the cell can characterise policy but cannot position for invitation. Resolving this is the highest-leverage next step, and it likely requires human/commercial channels rather than web collection.

negative_findings.description: Group-level procurement doctrine that governs Czech sourcing — Erste Group Procurement, KBC group supplier policy, SG responsible sourcing, RBI group code — is published predominantly in English or German. Czech-language equivalents exist only where the local bank republishes them (KB's Czech PDF stack, rb.cz's Czech slug). Erste's general supplier page states country-translated documents exist behind a drop-down, but I could not reach the Czech variant with a non-rendering fetch.
negative_findings.result_summary: Local-language coverage is good at bank level (KB, Moneta, rb.cz, ČSOB) but thin at the group level that actually decides.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: A cs-only collection strategy would miss the layer where CZ sourcing decisions are genuinely made; an en-only strategy would miss the binding local contract terms. Both languages are required, and the Erste country drop-down specifically needs a rendering fetcher.

negative_findings.description: No Czech bank was found listed as a zadavatel (contracting authority) on any Czech e-procurement platform — TENDER ARENA, proebiz/profily.proebiz.com, or JOSEPHINE. Searching these platforms with banking terms returned only platform help documentation and public-sector contracts, including a public-sector 'poptávkové řízení - poskytnutí úvěru' where a bank is the BIDDER, not the buyer.
negative_findings.result_summary: No target bank identified as a buyer on any CZ e-procurement platform.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: Confirms the cell rationale empirically: private systemic banks bypass Czech public portals entirely. Also flags an inversion trap — banks appear on these portals frequently as suppliers of credit to public bodies, which must not be mistaken for bank procurement.

coverage_gaps.description: The Erste Group Procurement Czech subsidiary — the entity that actually buys on behalf of Česká spořitelna — has not been identified by legal name, IČO, or registered address. The alias 's ProServ' surfaced via LinkedIn but was not verified against a register.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Query the Czech commercial register (justice.cz / ARES) for Erste Group Procurement and s ProServ variants to obtain the CZ legal entity, IČO, address, statutory officers and filed financial statements. That entity, not csas.cz, is the correct monitoring target for ČS demand.

coverage_gaps.description: csob.cz is unreachable with a plain HTTP fetcher (uniform HTTP 500), leaving the largest CZ bank's procurement policy documented only through third-party corroboration.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Add a headless-browser / realistic-header fetch path for csob.cz to the collection pipeline, then re-attempt the procurement policy PDF and enumerate sibling documents under /documents/10710/. Do not mark any csob.cz source dead on the basis of the current 500s.

coverage_gaps.description: No named, entry-resolved e-sourcing platform for any of the eight banks. This is the difference between knowing a bank's procurement philosophy and knowing when it is buying.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Pursue via non-web channels: procurement-tech vendor case studies and press releases naming Czech banks; procurement job ads on LinkedIn/StartupJobs/Jobs.cz which routinely name the sourcing tool in required skills; conference and CPO-interview material; and direct enquiry to each bank's procurement function. Also monitor Erste/SG/KBC/RBI IR and supplier pages for platform migration announcements.

coverage_gaps.description: Air Bank, Partners Banka, Fio banka and UniCredit CZ have no discoverable supplier channel — four of eight named banks with effectively zero coverage.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Switch method for these: (a) search each for the legally mandated 'informační memorandum pro dodavatele' / supplier GDPR notice, which exists even without a supplier page and exposes the P2P data model — this technique worked for ČSOB Pojišťovna; (b) mine annual reports and CSRD sustainability statements for supply-chain sections; (c) map procurement staff via professional networks; (d) for Air Bank, follow the PPF group layer and the ongoing ČSOB ownership change, which may migrate its sourcing into the KBC framework.

coverage_gaps.description: The Czech-language supplier document set on Erste Group's site is behind a JavaScript country drop-down that a non-rendering fetch cannot expand, so the cs Supplier Code of Conduct and General Terms and Conditions of Purchase applicable to Česká spořitelna were not retrieved.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Render https://www.erstegroup.com/en/about-us/subsidiaries/erste-group-procurement/general with a headless browser, expand the Czech Republic node, and harvest the cs PDFs; then locate their sibling paths under /content/dam/ for direct future fetching.

coverage_gaps.description: Only current versions of supplier codes and terms were located; no historical versions or change logs. Without a baseline, the diff-based monitoring recommended for KB, KBC, Erste and RBI cannot detect the first change it sees.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Seed the archive now by capturing every identified policy PDF, and backfill prior versions from web.archive.org for kb.cz/cs/dodavatele, kbc.com/en/our-suppliers, rb.cz supplier code, and the Erste EGP pages. Establish version hashes as the monitoring baseline.

coverage_gaps.description: The cell has no route to award-level or spend-level data. No CZ private bank publishes contract awards, supplier lists, or category spend, and none appears on public e-procurement platforms as a buyer.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Substitute indirect evidence: incumbent-vendor press releases and reference customers (the strongest available award proxy); CSRD sustainability statements which may disclose supplier counts and screening rates; and the subsidy exception documented in the MPO rulebook — set a standing watch for subsidised-project tenders naming bank entities, the one path by which a private bank purchase becomes a public notice.

coverage_gaps.description: Pointer-class sources are thin. Only one genuinely productive Czech pointer was found (byznysprospolecnost.cz / byznysudrzitelnost.cz), and it was discovered incidentally rather than systematically.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Systematically work the Czech responsible-business and procurement-professional ecosystem: Byznys pro společnost, Asociace pro veřejné zakázky, Česká bankovní asociace, and Czech procurement trade media. These publish bank-procurement interviews naming staff and describing internal process — the richest open substitute for a supplier portal in this cell.

brief: Czech systemic banks publish supplier POLICY, never supplier DEMAND: across all eight targets I found codes of conduct, general purchase terms and responsible-purchasing charters, but not a single RFP, tender notice or award notice on any bank channel, and no target bank appears as a buyer on TENDER ARENA, proebiz or JOSEPHINE. The decisive structural finding is that sourcing is largely not local — Česká spořitelna's external spend runs through Erste Group Procurement (which has its own Czech subsidiary, hence no supplier page on csas.cz at all), ČSOB is bound by the KBC group supplier policy, KB by Société Générale's charter and online-only sourcing process, and Raiffeisenbank by the RBI group code; only KB and rb.cz maintain a genuine Czech-language supplier-facing page, while Moneta files its supplier ethics code among ordinary downloads and Air Bank, Partners, Fio and UniCredit CZ publish nothing at all. Practical consequences for collection: csob.cz returned HTTP 500 on every attempt and needs a headless-browser fetch path (unverified, not dead), Erste's Czech supplier documents sit behind a JS country drop-down, and no bank's actual e-sourcing platform could be named or entry-resolved — the single highest-leverage gap. Until that platform layer is cracked, the usable signal in this cell comes from policy-document diffs, group-level ESG/CSRD supply-chain disclosure, procurement-tech vendor case studies, and Czech responsible-business interviews such as Byznys pro společnost's ČSOB piece, which remains the richest open description of how a Czech bank actually tenders.
